title: BIBFRAME domains and ranges, read as constraints
$comment:
GENERATED by generate/from_ontology.py. Do not edit.

From BIBFRAME 3.0.1, issued 2025-12-03T12:00:00-05:00.

rdfs:domain and rdfs:range are inference rules under OWL and cannot be violated; this reads them as constraints instead, which is the flip SHACL makes. Violations are warnings rather than errors: when the data and the ontology disagree, the ontology is often the one that is behind.

x-skipped.domain ensembleSize: declares bf:Work; every use is on bf:Ensemble, as with mediumComponent.
x-skipped.domain mediumComponent: declares bf:Work; every use is on bf:Ensemble, which is not a Work subclass. Music modelling the ontology has not caught up with.
x-skipped.range mediumOfPerformance: declares bf:MediumOfPerformance; every use points at mads:Medium, a class from a vocabulary BIBFRAME does not reference.
x-skipped.domain relief: declares bf:Instance; every use is on bf:Cartographic, a Work. The ontology looks simply wrong -- relief is a work-level characteristic. Worth reporting upstream.

literal.$comment: rdfs:range rdfs:Literal: a literal rather than a reference. A plain string, number or boolean passes, and so does a value object; only a node with an @id fails.
